sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:45893
Court No. - 76

Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 2345 of 2024
Applicant :- Ajmal

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Sarve Nazir,Zafar Abbas
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1. Sri Rajiv Dhar Dwivedi, learned Aga apprised the Court that he has received the instructions,
therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be finally, disposed off.
2. Heard Sri Zafar Abbas, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajiv Dhar Dwivedi, learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No. 26 of 2024, under Sections 392 IPC, Police Station Kotwalishaher, District Bijnor, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail, till the conclusion of trial.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against unknown persons and according to the FIR three unknown persons snatched the mobile phone of the informant.
5.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that nobody was named in the FIR but during investigation, one co-accused Aman was apprehended and from his possession, looted mobile of the Ajmal vs State Of U.P. on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132076086/
1 informant was recovered and he disclosed the name of the applicant.
6.
He further submitted that except the statement of co-accused Aman, there is no other evidence against the applicant on record.

7. He next submitted that co-accused Aman is highly enemical with the applicant and in the year 2013 mother of the applicant has lodged a NCR against the co-accused Aman and his father which has been annexed as annexure-4 to the affidavit filed alongwith the instant anticipatory bail application.

8. He further submitted that even the mother of the co-accused Aman also lodged a false case of section 376 IPC against the brother of the applicant and this fact is evident from annexure-5 to the affidavit.
9. He further submitted that only due to this enmity applicant has been falsely implicated by the co-accused Aman in the present matter.

10. He further submitted that applicant was having no previous criminal history to his credit but on the basis of statement of co-accused Aman he was simultaneously made accused in two cases including present one and in both the cases, name of applicant was disclosed through the statement of co-accused Aman.
11. He further submitted that investigation of the case is pending and police is trying to arrest the applicant.
12. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail but could not dispute the arguments on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
13. I have heard learned counsel for both the sides and perused the record of the case.

14. FIR of the present case was lodged against unknown persons and name of the applicant was surfaced in the present matter through the statement of co-accused and from annexure nos. 4 and 5 of the affidavit it appears that the applicant and co-accused Aman were having animosity and therefore, argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant cannot be completely ruled out.

15. However, it appears that apart from the present case, applicant is having criminal history of one another case but in that case, applicant was also made accused on the basis of statement made by co-accused Aman.
16.
Further, investigation of the case is pending and apprehension of arrest raised by the applicant cannot be ruled out.

17. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in this case, till conclusion of trial.

Ajmal vs State Of U.P. on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132076086/
2 18.
Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

21. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

Order Date :- 14.3.2024 Ankita  Ajmal vs State Of U.P. on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132076086/
